correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact three-type peripheral-pair dynamics. Type a frozen h/h, type b frozen !h/!h, mixed m becomes h/h after one update. Hub flips first iff b>a, ultimately iff b>n/2 or at b=n/2 after first flip. This gives fixed by round two, n>=3 sharp, initial/terminal global-majority identities, reversal iff a<b<n/2, and 2^n+1_even*C(n,n/2) fixed points. Under unbiased independent pair types (1/4,1/4,1/2), a=b diagonal has probability C(2n,n)/4^n; b~Bin(n,1/4) gives permanent-flip tail with the sole exceptional even tie. Geometric tail ratios and Stirling give the displayed exponential factor and R_n=1/2-1/(2sqrt(pi n))+O(n^-3/2). Under conditional Bernoulli(p), signed pair mean 2p-1 and variance 1/2 at p=1/2; binomial p² crosses 1/2 at p=1/sqrt(2). Both triangular-array Gaussian windows have Phi(2sqrt(2)s). Independently enumerated labelled states n<=6 and verified exact formulas; the universal conclusion relies on algebra/CLT, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Natural symmetric majority network exhibits a previously non-obvious transient majority reversal in asymptotically half of uniform states despite exponentially rare permanent hub flip; the intermediate bias phase flips then reverts with probability tending to one. limitations: Only synchronous binary strict neighbor majority with current-state tie retention; not random tie breaking, self-loops, asynchronous dynamics or arbitrary topologies.
